messages:
julie_support: quick heads-up / support just routed two escalations — customers report sudden p95/p99 increases after last night's runtime rollout (v1.4.2). No error traces, just much higher tails. Can runtime / infra triage? :interrobang:

mike_runtime: which customers and which endpoints? any request IDs?

julie_support: Customer-Atlas and Customer-Beta, mostly the /generate route (text gen) and a couple embedding requests. They saw p95 jump from ~100ms to ~300-450ms and p99 up near 1.1s. First reports around 2023-11-13T03:50Z (post-deploy).

deploy-bot: deployed runtime v1.4.2 -> pool:prod at 2023-11-13T03:30Z by @mike_runtime

emma_sre: quick PromQL checks coming up:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
```

mike_runtime: running those now 1030Z metrics show cluster p95 increased to ~340ms right after 03:30. Canary nodes 410ms p95; legacy nodes ~110ms.

sanjay_prod: what changed in 1.4.2? I recall a kernel dispatch change and a batching tweak.

mike_runtime: correct 1: kernel-dispatch v2 (prefers fused kernels for mid-length sequences) and adaptive_batcher default window increased to 18ms to favor throughput. Both controlled by env flags.

emma_sre: before we rollback, can we flip flags on the canary pool? that'd isolate quick.

mike_runtime: both flags are runtime-configurable: KERNEL_DISPATCH=2 and ADAPTIVE_BATCH_MS=18. I'll reduce ADAPTIVE_BATCH_MS to 4 on canary and watch.

deploy-bot: updating pool:canary env ADAPTIVE_BATCH_MS -> 4 (in progress)

mike_runtime: change applied. Observing.

emma_sre: within ~3m the canary p95 dropped from 410ms to ~150ms; p99 fell from ~900ms to ~320ms.

sanjay_prod: that strongly implicates the batching window. kernel-dispatch might still influence p99 for certain sequence-length buckets.

mike_runtime: agreed. For immediate customer-facing mitigation we'll keep ADAPTIVE_BATCH_MS=4 cluster-wide and keep KERNEL_DISPATCH on a controlled subset while we dig deeper.

julie_support: telling customers: "We've applied a temporary config change that reduced tail latency; full RCA in progress." They want ETA on permanent fix.

tara_oncall: propose we run an AB matrix in an isolated test pool:
- baseline (v1.4.1)
- v1.4.2 with only batching change
- v1.4.2 with only kernel-dispatch change
- v1.4.2 with both
use synthetic bursty load that mirrors their traffic shape.

mike_runtime: I'll spin that up. reproducer (bash):
```
TOKEN=redwood-test-token
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -X POST "https://internal.test/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"open-llm/q8_0","input":"test payload","max_tokens":48}' &
  sleep 0.008
done
wait
```

mike_runtime: quick run results:
- baseline (v1.4.1) p95 ~105ms, p99 ~200ms
- batching-only p95 ~360ms, p99 ~700ms
- kernel-dispatch-only p95 ~125ms, p99 ~260ms
- both p95 ~420ms, p99 ~840ms

emma_sre: plots show queue_depth and held_requests spike proportionally when ADAPTIVE_BATCH_MS is 18. mean batch size grows and tail latency increases under bursty arrivals.

sanjay_prod: so adaptive batching increases throughput but harms tail when arrivals are bursty. kernel-dispatch amplifies p99 for certain token-lengths.

tara_oncall: immediate actions:
- set ADAPTIVE_BATCH_MS=4 globally
- add a max_hold_ms parameter (suggest 10ms) to cap how long requests are held
- enable kernel-dispatch only on a small traffic slice with sequence-length regression tests
- add a metric gate: auto-rollback if p95 > 200ms for 5m post-rollout

mike_runtime: implemented max_hold_ms and a burst-detect circuit that disables enlargement of the batch window when inter-arrival variance is high. PR: https://git.internal.redwood/runtime/pull/511

deploy-bot: PR 511 merged into main; deploying canary config

mike_runtime: rolling config to canary with metric gating.

emma_sre: also added an alert rule to catch tail regressions earlier:
```
alert: RuntimeTailRegression
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/generate"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.2
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "/generate p95 > 200ms"
```

sanjay_prod: add release-note line and tag in case support needs to reference mitigation steps.

julie_support: customers updated; Customer-Beta confirmed improved tail after the config change. They appreciate the quick mitigation.

mike_runtime: root-cause summary for incident: adaptive-batching window expansion held requests during short bursts leading to head-of-line p95 degradation; kernel-dispatch contributed to p99 in narrow sequence-length bands but wasn't the primary driver.

tara_oncall: follow-ups: RFC for safer adaptive-batcher defaults (default 4ms, max_hold_ms 10ms), integrate tail-focused smoke tests into the release pipeline, and run a kernel-dispatch perf matrix across sequence-lengths and model quantization types. I'll open the incident ticket and assign owners.

julie_support: closing the customer escalations after posting the mitigation notes and ETA for the RFC. thanks all :clap:
